technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment in the existing Hyperledger Fabric codebase, using Go for peer, orderer, chaincode lifecycle, cache, and CLI changes.
Represent a chaincode friendly name as persisted lifecycle metadata and expose it through the existing administrative/query APIs without changing the chaincode package identity.

Use the lifecycle system chaincode as the authoritative mechanism for storing and enforcing chaincode deployment and upgrade policies, with policy evaluation performed through existing Fabric policy and endorsement infrastructure.
Implement Solo ordering as a single-process orderer using an in-memory input queue, one batching goroutine, an in-memory block ledger, and per-client seekable delivery.
Use explicit block-number and transaction-position cursors for delivery history, allowing clients to disconnect and resume from a previously requested position.
Provide the state cache through a peer-internal API that supports read access to cached committed state and is safe for concurrent transaction simulation requests.
Extract administrative peer commands into a standalone CLI package with no dependency on the validating peer runtime or RocksDB.
Publish the source repository through a GitHub mirror or canonical GitHub repository and add project-level documentation navigation linking Fabric documentation from hyperledger.org.
Use unit tests for isolated components and integration tests for lifecycle, Solo ordering, state cache, and CLI workflows; preserve existing APIs unless a new API is required by the stories.
assumptions: The existing Fabric repository, build system, protobuf definitions, policy engine, peer, orderer, and chaincode lifecycle foundations are available and buildable.
The increment is implemented by one software developer; estimates represent active work effort and exclude elapsed calendar time, staffing delays, and external approvals.
Requirements do not specify backward compatibility details, so existing behavior is preserved and new functionality is additive wherever practical.
The Solo orderer is intended for development and testing rather than production fault tolerance, persistence, or multi-node consensus.
The Solo in-memory ledger is allowed to lose all blocks on process restart; durable ledger recovery is out of scope.
The chaincode deployment policy model can reuse existing Fabric policy types, serialization, and signature validation mechanisms.
The state cache is an optimization and is not the authoritative ledger; cache invalidation follows committed block processing and stale-cache handling is covered by tests.
GitHub publication and hyperledger.org documentation navigation require repository and website access, but no major redesign of those external platforms.
Cross-platform CLI support targets the principal developer platforms supported by the existing build system, including Linux, macOS, and Windows.
Security hardening, production operational tooling, performance benchmarking beyond functional acceptance, and unrelated refactoring are out of scope.

activities.activity_description: Trace all eight user stories to the existing Fabric components, define interfaces and data flows, identify compatibility impacts, and produce an implementation and test plan.
Add lifecycle metadata and persistence for a human-readable chaincode name, update administrative/query APIs and serialization, and implement validation and error handling.
Extend the lifecycle system chaincode to create, update, retrieve, and enforce chaincode deployment or upgrade policies using the existing Fabric policy model and authorization flow.
Add unit and integration tests covering metadata persistence, policy authorization, valid and invalid upgrades, policy failures, and compatibility with existing lifecycle operations.
Document chaincode installation, approval or deployment policy changes, upgrade sequencing, failure handling, rollback considerations, and representative command or API flows.
Implement the single-process ordering path with buffered transaction intake, serialized batching, block construction, configuration handling, lifecycle management, and orderer service integration.

activities.activity_name: Solo in-memory ledger and seekable delivery
activities.activity_description: Implement in-memory block retention, block-number and cursor lookup, client-specific delivery streams, disconnect/reconnect behavior, bounds checking, and concurrent access control.

activities.activity_name: Solo orderer tests and developer configuration
activities.activity_description: Add unit, service-level, and integration tests for ordering, batching, delivery, history seeking, reconnection, concurrent clients, malformed requests, and development-network configuration.

Design and implement the state-cache storage and lookup API, integrate it with transaction simulation and committed-state updates, and handle misses, invalidation, concurrency, and lifecycle behavior.

activities.activity_name: State cache tests and performance validation
activities.activity_description: Test cache hits and misses, invalidation after commits, concurrent access, stale data prevention, restart behavior, and basic performance improvement for read/write-set construction.
Prepare the repository for GitHub discovery, configure or validate mirroring and branch visibility, add contribution and source navigation information, and verify that the published code is usable.
Organize or add developer documentation indexes for chaincode and application development and add links or navigation from the Hyperledger project documentation entry point.

Separate peer administrative commands from validating-peer internals, define stable command interfaces, remove unnecessary RocksDB and node-runtime dependencies, and implement component interaction through public APIs.
Add platform-specific builds and packaging for Linux, macOS, and Windows, provide installation and usage documentation, and verify that the resulting binary can interact with the Fabric components.
Test command parsing, component connectivity, lifecycle and channel operations, error reporting, binary installation, and regression behavior against existing administrative workflows.

activities.activity_name: End-to-end integration, regression, and release preparation
activities.activity_description: Run the complete build and test suite, exercise combined lifecycle, Solo ordering, cache, and CLI scenarios, fix integration defects, update release notes, and prepare the increment for delivery.
